newsitem.title: USA: Sears sees December same-store sales gain.
newsitem.headline: Sears sees December same-store sales gain.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co. expects its December same-store retail sales to be up about six percent from last year, Arthur Martinez, the company's chairman and chief executive, said on Monday.
"I think consumers are in a buying mood," Martinez said following an address to the Economic Club of Detroit.

Last year, U.S. retail industry sales on a comparable-store basis rose about two percent, he said, while Sears' sales climbed six percent. "I think the industry is going to do better this year, and I think we're on track to match last year's six percent increase," he said.
Healthy sales last weekend indicate the holiday buying season got off to a strong start, Martinez said. He said sales of apparel are leading the growth.
"Judging off this weekend's business -- the kind of traffic and activity I saw this weekend -- customers are ready to do business," he said.

Martinez credited manageable levels of consumer debt and stable interest rates for this season's good prospects. He noted the late date of the Thanksgiving holiday is expected to have an effect on both November and December sales by pushing more business into December.
"December is going to be even more action-packed than normal, if that's possible," he said.

In response to a question, Martinez said Sears, the nation's second-largest retailer, is increasingly optimistic about urban retail activity and would consider putting a store in downtown Detroit if it finds the right location.

Sears has its hands full trying to build its business in North America, Martinez said, and does not view international growth as a top priority. He said international expansion is "number six on my top five list."

Martinez, who joined the Chicago-based company in September 1992 as the head of its retail arm, described during his prepared remarks how Sears has rebuilt its business by refocusing on women customers, renovating stores, upgrading service and changing its marketing approach.
He also stressed how Sears changed its internal culture by implementing programs that boosted morale and pushed decision-making to lower ranks.
"Arrogance is a mortal sin, and it almost did in our company," he said.
